title: Coconut wax and frankincense candle
subtitle: A creamy, slow-burning jar candle
excerpt: A container candle made with coconut wax and frankincense essential oil. Coconut wax burns more slowly than soy and produces a creamier white finish. The frankincense gives a warm, resinous scent. Makes one 200 ml jar.
sourceNotes: Coconut wax properties and pour temperature: supplier data sheets and general candlemaking reference. Frankincense (Boswellia carterii) essential oil in candlemaking: general aromatherapy reference. IFRA guidelines for frankincense EO.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~200 ml jar, ~40 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Four or five jars per session.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years unlit in a cool, dark place. Frankincense essential oil is relatively stable in wax and holds its scent well.

glossaryTerms.definition: A natural wax made from hydrogenated coconut oil. Slightly higher melt point than soy wax (around 50°C), slower burning, and produces a very creamy, smooth finish. Good fragrance throw. Pour temperature is 55 to 60°C.

content.text: scented with frankincense essential oil. Coconut wax sets with a creamy, smooth surface and burns slightly more slowly than soy; the jar often lasts five to ten hours longer than a comparable soy candle. Frankincense gives a dry, warm, resinous note suited to quiet work spaces and winter evenings.
Never leave a burning candle unattended.

items.prepNote: pre-tabbed cotton wick for a 200 ml jar

content.text: Warm the jar. Fix the wick centred in the base. Melt the coconut wax over a bain-marie. Cool to 58°C. Add the frankincense essential oil and stir for one minute. Pour into the jar. Leave overnight. Trim the wick to 5 mm. Cure for one week before lighting.
Allow the melt pool to reach the jar edge on the first burn. Coconut wax is slower to melt than soy; the first burn may take three to four hours to reach the edge of a 200 ml jar.
Two years unlit in a cool, dark place.
